source.title: Insights from Gradient Dynamics: Gradient Autoscaled Normalization

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some equations and figure content are flattened or missing, so precise plotted values cannot be recovered.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses its observations about gradient statistics to develop a gradient-normalization method, then reports test accuracy and convergence comparisons for that method. It does not test the claim versions’ training-error outcomes or named conditions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracy for its proposed gradient normalization and comparison methods, but not training classification error. Those accuracy results do not measure the behavior in the claim versions and are not included as rows. It also reports gradient-standard-deviation measurements during training; those are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study uses residual and batch-normalized CNN backbones to evaluate its gradient transformation. It measures gradient statistics and test accuracy, without comparing initialization, shortcuts, batch normalization, width-related local minima, training-error attainment, or learning-rate stability thresholds. Gradient normalization is not batch normalization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors use observed gradient dynamics to motivate autoscaled gradient normalization and claim reduced amplification and improved generalization. On CIFAR-100, their method improves reported test accuracy for both ResNets and matches the VGG baseline; these results do not establish any listed claim version.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes a gradient transformation combining layer-wise mean removal with a shared global autoscale; its experiments use AdamW. It does not use the claim versions’ stated training-error tests.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports architecture-dependent layer-wise gradient-standard-deviation patterns. It also says the Z-Score method can amplify low-standard-deviation layers, especially in VGG, and may degrade performance or diverge.

fits_no_version.finding: Across ResNet-20, ResNet-56 and VGG-16-BN on CIFAR-10, global gradient standard deviation decreases during training, while layer-wise trends vary.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Global gradient standard deviation can decline during CNN training despite heterogeneous layer-wise trends.

record.problems: The reported gradient-statistic values are presented in figures without recoverable numerical values in the supplied text. The CIFAR-100 results report test accuracy, not training classification error. No uncertainty estimates are stated for the reported experiments.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 and Figure 4 compare test accuracy and convergence for the proposed method and other normalization methods on CIFAR-100. These results do not report training classification error or directly test any listed version, so they were not extracted as rows.

untested.parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, and dependence on model size, stopping time or regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima and extra student neurons.
Depth-related training degradation, matched shortcut comparisons, deep plain tanh initialization and normalization-free residual training.
Initialization effects on learning speed, signal propagation and trainable depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Recovery above initial stability thresholds, curvature changes, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence conditions.
Batch normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Table 1 and Figure 4 are already declared in rows_left_out. The scaled-SGD analysis assumes a bounded effective step size and does not test recovery above a stability threshold.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, including with corrupted or random labels; model size, training duration, early stopping and regularized recipes.
Teacher-student local minima and student width relative to teacher width.
Depth effects on training error, identity shortcuts, special initialization for deep plain networks and normalization-free residual training.
Initialization comparisons and their effects on training speed or trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, recovery, sharpness and divergence.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.
